text:
Dear Partners,

The quarter unfolded much as the tape suggested it would: a quiet session on the wire, data prints in line, and a market that seems content, for now, to sit still. The central bank held its policy rate at 5.00%, inflation continues its slow normalization at 2.9%, and high-yield spreads settled at 400bps — wide enough to remind the market that credit discipline matters, narrow enough to confirm that the panic of prior quarters has passed. We read this as a market catching its breath rather than one signaling distress. Commentary on the wire this quarter struck a similarly measured tone, and we think that measured posture is the correct one.

Turning to the portfolio: our NAV index stands at 101.1, and we are pleased to report a reported return of +1.1% for the quarter, matching our year-to-date figure of +1.1%, and continuing to build on a since-inception return of +33.0% that remains the truest measure of what this strategy delivers across a cycle. Public equities returned +1.3% over the same period — a gap of a few tenths that we view as noise rather than signal, well within the range one would expect given the differing cadence of private and public marks. We do not chase quarterly beta; we build businesses.

Portfolio company performance continues to validate our underwriting. Operating teams have pushed through pricing actions and working-capital discipline at several of our larger holdings, and the results are showing up in EBITDA conversion even as headline financing costs remain elevated. Where financing costs have bitten, we continue to view this as temporary dislocation in the capital markets rather than any structural repricing of the assets themselves. Refinancing conversations with counterparties remain constructive, and we expect maturity walls across the vintage to be addressed methodically rather than urgently.

Looking ahead, we remain constructive but not complacent. Should credit conditions tighten further, or should defaults rise across the broader leveraged market, we would expect dispersion between well-managed operating businesses and financially engineered ones to widen — a dynamic we believe favors our approach. We continue to watch the pace of rate normalization closely, as a prudent operator must, and we are mindful that a market this quiet can turn quickly. Our conviction is that the fundamentals underlying this vintage remain sound, though we acknowledge the path to full realization may take longer than entry multiples once implied.

We thank our limited partners for their continued partnership, and look forward to updating you next quarter.

Onward.

Meridian Capital Partners
